explanation: Retrospective, largely sense-blind lexical detector that fires on the word itself for a small set of personal-life words (house, home, school, kitchen, apartment, childhood, born, married, memoir, autobi-ography) and words for speaking (say/saying, talked, interview), but only when the word stands after a preposition, possessive or verb, or follows 'to/would' or a percent-of-people subject (in a school, his parents' house, left home, refused to say, 21 per cent say); 'interview' fires in every position and sense, even in 'The interview questions for the test suite', and 'school' fires even in 'in a school of fish'. The same words are near zero as the first word of a sentence or as a modifier ('School was closed', 'Home is', 'the home button', 'The school board'), and in 'I can't say' and 'The data say'; capitalised 'House' (of Representatives) is low; impersonal or technical nouns (server, protein, equation, car, table, meeting) stay low; venues like hotel, airport, office and river sit around a quarter of max, near the threshold.
